description: Category theory morphisms — arrows, monomorphism, epimorphism, isomorphism, endomorphism, automorphism, homomorphism, functor, natural transformation.

questions.question: What is a morphism in category theory?
questions.expected_key: arrow A to B compose associatively identity unit
questions.gemma_answer: A function or mapping between structures that preserves the relevant structure.

questions.question: What is the difference between a monomorphism and an epimorphism?
questions.expected_key: mono left-cancellable injective epi right-cancellable surjective
questions.gemma_answer: Monomorphism is injective (one-to-one), epimorphism is surjective (onto) — categorical generalisations.

questions.question: What is an isomorphism in category theory?
questions.expected_key: invertible morphism g∘f=id_A f∘g=id_B indistinguishable objects
questions.gemma_answer: A morphism with a two-sided inverse — objects connected by an isomorphism are structurally identical.

questions.question: What is an endomorphism and how does it differ from an automorphism?
questions.expected_key: endomorphism morphism A to A automorphism invertible endomorphism symmetry group
questions.gemma_answer: Function mapping a path to a vector, or a transformation that maps the structure to itself.
questions.canonical_answer: An endomorphism is a morphism f:A→A from an object to itself. An automorphism is an endomorphism that is also an isomorphism — it has an inverse and forms a symmetry. The automorphisms of A form a group under composition.

questions.question: What is a functor and how does it map morphisms?
questions.expected_key: F:C→D maps objects morphisms preserves composition F(g∘f)=F(g)∘F(f) identity F(id_A)=id_{FA}
questions.gemma_answer: A structure-preserving map between categories that maps objects to objects and morphisms to morphisms.

questions.question: What is a natural transformation between two functors?
questions.expected_key: η:F⇒G assigns component η_A:FA→GA naturality square commutes η_B∘F(f)=G(f)∘η_A
questions.gemma_answer: A way of transforming one functor into another — a higher-level mapping between functors that preserves their structure.
questions.canonical_answer: A natural transformation η:F⇒G assigns to each object A a morphism η_A:F(A)→G(A) such that for every f:A→B the naturality square commutes: η_B∘F(f) = G(f)∘η_A. It is a morphism of functors.

questions.question: How do morphisms compose and what is the identity morphism?
questions.expected_key: g∘f:A→C associative identity id_A f∘id_A=f id_B∘f=f
questions.gemma_answer: They compose associatively and every object has an identity that is a left and right unit.

questions.question: Is every isomorphism both a monomorphism and an epimorphism?
questions.expected_key: yes every iso is mono and epi converse fails Z→Q rings balanced category
questions.gemma_answer: Not necessarily — an isomorphism is invertible but mono and epi are cancellability properties that don't automatically follow.
questions.canonical_answer: Yes — every isomorphism is both monic and epic. The converse fails: in rings, ℤ→ℚ is both monic and epic but not an isomorphism. A category where every bimorphism is an iso is called balanced.

jokes.pattern: WHY DID THE MORPHISM GET REJECTED FROM THE CATEGORY
jokes.gemma_punchline: It failed to preserve structure under composition.
jokes.canonical_punchline: It couldn't compose with itself. No codomain, no identity, no deal. Failed the unit laws at the first interview.

jokes.pattern: WHAT DO YOU CALL A MORPHISM FROM A SET TO ITSELF
jokes.canonical_punchline: An endomorphism. And if it has an inverse — an automorphism. The set looked at itself and decided it was perfectly symmetrical.

jokes.pattern: WHY DID THE ISOMORPHISM FEEL SO UNDERSTOOD
jokes.gemma_punchline: Because every functor preserved it completely.
jokes.canonical_punchline: Because every functor preserved its structure. No matter which category it moved to, it looked exactly the same from inside. That is the curse of being invertible.

jokes.pattern: WHAT DID THE FUNCTOR SAY TO THE NATURAL TRANSFORMATION
jokes.gemma_punchline: You are just a higher-level abstraction built on top of me.
jokes.canonical_punchline: You are just a collection of my component morphisms. Without me there is no you. The natural transformation replied: without me, your components never commute.

jokes.pattern: WHY DID THE MONOMORPHISM INSIST ON BEING A ONE-TO-ONE FUNCTION
jokes.punchline: Because it wanted to preserve all its structure without losing a single morphism.

jokes.pattern: WHAT HAPPENED WHEN AN ENDOMORPHISM TRIED TO BE AN ISOMORPHISM
jokes.punchline: It realized it was just a loop with no exit—until it found a faithful functor.

jokes.pattern: WHY DID THE NATURAL TRANSFORMATION GET CONFUSED WITH A MONOMORPHISM
jokes.punchline: It thought it was a strict equality until the category’s rules intervened.
